correctness.rationale: A complete width-four row-state dynamic program exactly minimizes total dominating sets after edge deletions and exhausts every isolate-free one-, two-, and three-edge set at lengths 5,7,8. The admissible/damaging cut counts for sizes 1..3 are (31/0,461/0,4369/40), (45/0,986/0,14004/727), and (52/0,1322/0,21884/0). Explicit 3-,3-,4-edge witnesses raise gamma_t from 8 to 9, 10 to 11, and 12 to 13. The separate original-optimum enumerator lists 256,121,2916 minimum total dominating sets and reproduces all cut counts by selected-neighbor survival tests, invoking the exact monotonicity equivalence. Both executable source files and their outputs are included. This is finite exhaustive proof, not an induction over arbitrary lengths.

value.rationale: The 2011 total-bondage study explicitly isolates unresolved four-column residue classes with upper bounds. Lengths 5,7,8 are the first natural test cases of the classes 0,2,3 modulo 5 and fill the three initial exact-value gaps. The length-8 evaluation proves the proposed four-cut robustness bound sharp for the first possible instance, length 7 proves its three-cut bound sharp, and length 5 improves four to three. The counts 40 and 727 quantify how frequently optimum total domination fails under minimal edge losses. This directly answers an existing mathematical vulnerability question, not an arbitrary induced-subgraph selection or a standard known-table recomputation.
